entityDescription:
University of Ioannina participates in the development of several research projects in the research areas of science, chemistry, new materials, economic studies, biochemistry, biology, medicine, biomedicine, nursing care, environment, agriculture, education technologies and science, arts, as well as information and communication technologies.
All funded research activities are coordinated by the University of Ioannina Research Committee (UOI-RC), whose main aim is to manage the National, EU and industrial research projects in accordance to National and EU financial regulations, as well as ISO 9001:2015 standards. 
The aim of the University of Ioannina Research Committee is the management of funds, which come from any source and are intended to cover expenses of any kind, essential for the needs of research, educational, training and developmental projects as well as for the needs of continuous training projects. These funds can also cover expenses of projects that provide scientific and technological services, the elaboration of special studies, the implementation of tests, measurements, laboratory exams and analyses, consultations, as well as other related services or activities that contribute to the connection between education and research with the industry. These services and activities are implemented or provided by the scientific personnel of the University of Ioannina, in close collaboration with other specialists or external scientific personnel.
Furthermore, the aforementioned Quality Management System is compliant with the requirements of the Greek Management Efficiency Standard, in the scope of “Project Management of Research and Development of Technological and Other Related Programs and Activities”.

entityDescription:
CTIC Technology Centre (CTIC) is a private non-profit Research and Technology Organization (RTO), specialized in the research and development of cutting-edge and emerging technologies. Its main objective is to promote and foster the carrying out of activities related to the development of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in all spheres of economic and social life that may contribute to the development and improvement of society. Other strategic goals are to contribute to improve business competitiveness through applied research and innovation; to disseminate Science and Technology among citizens, companies and institutions; to help implement Information Society, Social Innovation and Development Cooperation policies; to contribute to the building of an inclusive knowledge society for both citizens and businesses; to provide high value-added technological services to society, businesses and public entities.
CTIC staff is formed by employees a team of >60 persons including engineers and PhD researchers specialized in ICT technologies, who generate high added-value knowledge through the research carried out in emerging IT fields and the proactive collaboration with national and international research groups. This allows to support business participation in innovative projects and to improve knowledge transfer between research institutions, industry and public administrations.
CTIC activity is focused on enabling technologies for digital transformation: Web of Things (WoT); Artificial Intelligence and Big Data; Standardization and Open Data; Vision Technologies and Blockchain. The research on these technologies aims to promote the intelligent and innovative development of territories; to improve business competitiveness through innovation and digital transformation (Industry 4.0); and contribute to improving people's quality of life.

description: Our company "2AM" is developing and producing high-strength aluminium wire (Almascan®) as a feedstock for Additive Manufacturing, also Metal Matrix Nano Composites for Aerospace Sector. Our team of professionals have worked on innovative lightweight Al-Mg-Sc alloys. The materials that are done already are high-strength profile materials of welded fuselage panels and thin sheet material for fibre metallic laminates and aircraft skin panels. Our primary mission is to continue Advanced Materials R&D activities, in 2020, we have got our own laboratory for testing existing and creating new materials and pilot production of the wire. In a near future, we are going to set up industrial production of high-strength aluminium wire for Additive Manufacturing. 3D printing with wire feedstock is one of the most promising technologies for the additive manufacturing of large parts, both in terms of production speed and costs. High-strength Al-Mg-Sc alloys best reveal the potential of this technology.

entityDescription:
AIDRO Hydraulics & 3D Printing is an Italian high-tech SME specialized on the design and manufacturing of hydraulic parts and metal devices, both by traditional technologies and by metal Additive Manufacturing (AM).
With 3.8m€ turnover and 15 employees, the company was founded almost 40 years ago as an engineering and manufacturing company for Fluid Power solutions, such as hydraulic valves, hydraulic manifolds, heat exchangers. In search of a market differentiation and pushed by the need to innovate, in 2016 metal AM was introduced as production process on top of existing core activities.AM is used to produce parts of new and existing products, bringing them value in terms of weight saving, customization, fast prototyping, function/component integration and material substitution. In few years, by experimenting and by doing, Aidro has become acknowledged for being a worldwide pioneer in combining Fluid Power, its core competence, to AM know-how. Moreover, AM proved to be an enabling technology for the company, opening new markets, like Oil & Gas and Aerospace. Leveraging its hands-on experience, the company became active member of international working groups focused on the definition of guidelines and standard for AM in Oil & Gas sector (Joint Innovation Program piloted by DNV GL and American Petroleum Institute). In 2018, Aidro obtained the aeronautical certification EN9100 and became member of the Lombardy Aerospace Cluster, a business network including prime and tier companies, which defined specific programs on AM for aerospace. Thanks to the new business relationship established, Aidro is now proving the viability of AM for very regulated industries and in some challenging applications, especially those where fluids under pressure flow in channels, specifically re-designed according to new concepts and free form geometries enabled by AM technology. In 2019, Aidro has been invited by EOS - Electro Optical System, the worldwide technology and market leader in AM, to join as a partner its ecosystem. Currently Aidro owns nr. 2 EOS M290 metal printers (LPBF) and has in-house design, post-finishing capacities and skilled engineers and operators.

entityDescription: At Beamagine we build solid-state imaging lidars for demanding applications, including all types of autonomous vehicles or high-accuracy inspection. The lack of moving elements provides L3CAM with the highest levels of robustness and long term stability in the market. Furthermore, it also provides the best capabilities in terms of balance of image resolution and frame rate on the market. Further, L3CAM may combine passive and active imaging modes in a single unit. The result is fused information without parallax errors, which you may call either an image with depth information, or a point cloud with colour information embedded. RGB, SWIR or polarimetric imaging modes are available and can be selected by the user. Units including IMUs or GPS are also available.

entityDescription:
SCASSI Conseil is a consulting and services company, specialized in information systems security domain.

We secure embedded and critical systems, from the design phase right up to the technical evaluation and accreditation phase.
Thanks to our dedicated Space and Defense Skills Center, we work on the ground segments or global system and cloud base architectures security, of main European missions and satellites (ISIS, GALILEO) to assist our manufacturer customers and space data managers in Europe.
We are involved in securing dual systems by deploying our industrialized methodologies of Risk & COTS Assessment, cyber-security management for complex projects, technical evaluation and hacking of embedded components or of business information systems.
Thanks to these projects, we have capitalized on sector-specific knowledge such as threats, standards (example), terminology & specific processes on which our Defense & Space Skills Center engineers are trained.
A few examples of projects carried out by SCASSI engineers:
- Risk analysis and technical support to secure space simulators
- EBIOS risk analysis relating to a complete system that offers services relating to space object management (SSA - Space Situational Awareness Programme)

- Study and securing of collaborative EDM/CMS type platforms handling sensitive information and for components of ground segments or payload
- Support program for security applications
- Cyber-security study for networks and data centers
- Support for accreditation of ground systems
- Support to secure technologies under Export Control
- Drafting of approval documentation
- Support towards Military Law conformity

entityDescription:
From Design to Manufacturing, OPT'ALM is a specific Metal Additive Manufacturing company with engineering and industrialisation expertise's, which works with its own machines on the DED laser Powder and Wire domains (DED AM).

OPT’ALM is connecting to the Industries of the Future to introduce Additive Manufacturing into production cycles of mechanical parts.
Located in Toulouse region, west south of France, OPT’ALM brings eco-production with a strong awareness of all industrial constraints.
We are replacing DED AM to traditional methods (sheet metal, casting, forging, machining) for specific parts in small series with high added value.
OPT’ALM's offer is divided into 3 fields of activity for leading-edge industries as spatial, by using the powder and wire laser DED AM :
1°) The repair and the Operation Condition Maintenance to suppress the scraps of mechanical parts and sub-assemblies,
2°) The process’s hybridization to add features on existing parts made from expensive and strategic raw materials,

KOMPAÏ Robotics’s main objective is to develop B2B robotics solutions to help people, not to replace them. We are active in several fields, such as Healthcare, Defense, Logistics, Cleanliness, Autonomous Vehicles … where we can develop prototypes or Proofs of Concept, imagine new use cases using service robots, or help to implement solutions.
One of our projects is to develop the Kompaï robots line of products, to help frail people and their caregivers, wherever they live.

entityDescription:
Cellnex Telecom is the main infrastructure operator for wireless telecommunication in Europe.
Cellnex has made a firm commitment to developing its network, which currently comprises c.128,000 sites, 71,000 of them already in the portfolio and the rest in the process of closing or planned roll-outs up to 2030 and positions the company to develop new generation networks. It provides services in Spain, Italy, Netherlands, United Kingdom, France, Switzerland, Ireland, Poland, Portugal, Austria, Denmark and Sweden thanks to the investments undertaken to boost its transformation and internationalisation drive.
Offers to its customers a range of services to guarantee the conditions for reliable and high-quality transmission of voice, data and audiovisual contents.
It also develops solutions in the field of “smart city” projects that optimise services to the citizen via networks and services that facilitate municipal management. In this area, Cellnex Telecom is deploying a network of intelligent communications that permits a connection between objects, and therefore the development of a solid ecosystem for the Internet of Things (IoT).
Cellnex Telecom also plays a relevant role in the deployment of safety and emergency networks for the security forces, known as PPDRs (Public Protection And Disaster Relief). This line of activity summarises both the degree of expertise the company’s team of professionals and the ruggedness and reliability of the architecture of its networks and equipment.
The company is listed on the continuous market of the Spanish stock exchange and is part of the selective IBEX 35, EuroStoxx 600 and MSCI Europe indices. It is also part of the FTSE4GOOD, CDP (Carbon Disclosure Project), Sustainalytics and “Standard Ethics” sustainability indexes.

entityDescription: Siemens Industry Software NV (SISW) runs the Simulation and Testing Solutions (STS) business unit of Siemens Digital Industries. SISW helps manufacturers worldwide across various industries bring innovative products to market faster and with greater confidence. For this purpose, SISW offers them a comprehensive environment, called Simcenter™ solutions, that uniquely combines test, system simulation, 3D CAE, CFD and design space exploration, as well as engineering services for those applications. By employing Simcenter solutions and services, major industry players in automotive, aviation and space, and various other mechatronic industries can be more effective during product ideation, when optimizing key performance aspects such as noise, vibrations, structural dynamics, durability, energy efficiency, safety, and more, while dealing with complexities such as ever-increasing mechatronics, additive manufacturing, and concepts like cloud or the internet of things. SISW created Simcenter after various strategic acquisitions of technology leaders in advanced performance engineering.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Flight Systems and Automatic Control (FSR) performs application oriented research in the area of aerospace systems engineering.
The current research topics are
-space traffic management & space safety
-concurrent engineering for complex technical systems
-future cockpit concepts
-unmanned aircraft systems
-prognostics and health management
-sustainable and efficient flight operations.

Many projects are carried out in close collaboration with space flight and aviation industry.

entityDescription:
Fraunhofer IGCV stands for application-driven research with focus on efficient engineering, networkedproduction and smart multi-material solutions. The institute drives innovation on the level of manufacturingprocesses and material sciences, machines and process chains as well as factory and enterprise networks. 
Our unique selling proposition lies in interdisciplinary solutions from the fields of casting, composite, and processing technology.

In an effort to transfer knowledge from research and development into industrial applications, our almost 160 employees at our locations in Augsburg and Munich/Garching generate individual solutions for Europes industry. As part of the Fraunhofer Group for Production – an association of production technology institutes – we support our partners with short-term, mid-term and long-term research projects. Thus, being a reliable partnerfor SMEs, large companies, and corporations we contribute to ensuring a sustainable competitive edge in Germany and Europe.

An abstract of our business and competence fields:

 Intelligent networking of production
 AI in production
 Additive manufacturing
 CFRP manufacturing technologies

o Automated-fiber-placement (AFP)
o Pultrusion
o Wet laid nonwoven

 Sand and gravity die casting
 Materials and testing technology
 Modeling and simulation
 Online process monitoring and quality-assured process chains
 Recycling
 Technology consulting and implementation
